name: Lantern Row lodging house
storeys: Four storeys plus a small attic
role: Narrow upper-town gaps and distant vertical accents
design: A TALL NARROW lodging house, FOUR full storeys plus a small attic under a steep front-facing terracotta gable. Approximately 4.5 m street frontage by 7 m deep. Clearly taller than it is wide: only two modest domestic windows across each upper frontage, one recessed dark-teal entry at ground level, limestone ground storey and faded warm cream/ochre plaster above. Simple oak floor bands, a shallow supported timber jetty at the second level, one small attic window in the gable and one slim brick chimney beside the rear-right roof edge. The right wall is relatively plain warm plaster, suitable for a neighbour standing close. Rear has two narrow window stacks, a modest ground service door and a low narrow tiled pantry projection at the foot of one side. A short washing line stays under the back eaves. Quiet residential character, clearly four full levels, no tower or public-building features. Roof and small chimney should give a useful thin skyline silhouette.
